newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African exchanges should merge, says JSE head.
newsitem.headline: S.African exchanges should merge, says JSE head.

text.p: The Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) should act quickly to merge with sister markets the South African Futures Exchange (Safex) and the South African Bond Exchange, JSE executive president Russell Loubser said on Wednesday.

Loubser told a news conference for the release of the JSE's 1996 annual report that changing South African legislation to allow such a move would probably take about two years, but interim agreements should be sealed before then.
"We don't have two years. We need some type of memorandum of understanding, letter of intent, whatever you want to call it...that can stand the test of time and the test of law," he said.
Calls for greater co-operation between the three markets are getting louder.

Earlier this month Stuart Rees, Safex's chief executive, said closer co-operation should be achieved by creating an umbrella body with the three financial exchanges as operating units, each retaining their independence and separate identity.

The JSE had a sickly year in terms of price performance in 1996, hit by a collapse in the value of the rand, which lost 29 percent of its value against the U.S. dollar last year and nearly 40 percent against the British pound.
The all-share index edged up 6.9 percent to 6,658, the all-gold index gained 12.1 percent to 1,506 and the industrials index dipped 0.8 percent to 7,922.
But there was an explosion in volume terms on the bourse and new listings were healthy.

The value of shares traded was up 85.6 percent to 117.4 billion rand and new capital raised was 28.4 billion rand, up from 19.5 billion rand in 1995. The average number of trades a day was up to 5,738 from 3,081.
Much of this burst of activity can be attributed the new computerised Jet trading system, which, after early faults, is smoothly up and running.

The system has helped boost liquidity of the market from 7.1 percent to 10.9 percent and Loubser said the trend was continuing with current liquidity levels around 14 percent. "Liquidity is definitely improving," he said.
